summary: Imperium: Classics is a card-driven civilization game where each player pilots one of eight asymmetric factions through its own custom deck, pruning starting cards for stronger ones as their civilization rises. Games feel like a tight, tactical duel of tempo, army-building, and card synergy rather than a sprawling 4X.
praised: solid solo mode against AI opponent decks
faster to teach than its depth suggests
criticised: some civilizations feel notably stronger than others
combat and card draw can feel swingy

interaction.kind: card-based raids and drafting from a shared market
interaction.detail: Players attack each other's civilizations with military cards and compete to draft cards from a shared market row, but each player otherwise builds and prunes their own personal deck independently.

scoring.how_you_win: You build up your civilization's deck by playing and trading cards for their icons/effects; when the era/event decks run out (or a player is forced into game-ending civil collapse) totals are tallied and the highest VP from cards and completed objectives wins.
